He would most likely be found **not guilty of arson**, because arson requires intent (or recklessness in some statutes), and forgetting a stove he had just used is at most negligence, since he was unaware of the risk. The "did not commit a felony" rationale is the wrong reason, because the acquittal turns on the missing mental state, not on whether a felony occurred, and "reckless" requires conscious disregard of a known risk, which he did not have.

CONFIDENCE: 70
